entries.message: fell back to a client render. This container's server markup was discarded and rebuilt (its template begins {template}; its SSR <style> is kept), so the page is correct but the server's work on it was wasted.
entries.fix: Its children are taken as server output of this template — if they were a client-side placeholder instead, empty the container first (`container.replaceChildren()`) or render the placeholder with vera. Otherwise the two renders have to agree exactly: check for markup the template does not describe, or state settled after the server render. Other containers on the page hydrate independently and are unaffected.

entries.message: there is no renderer to hydrate.
entries.fix: Wire it after the renderer: `wire([renderer, hydration])`.

entries.message: this @verajs/renderer and this hydration are from different releases. Pages render fresh (correct, without adopting the server's markup).
entries.fix: Update both together.

entries.message: this page was server-rendered with light-DOM slots, which hydration reads through `hydrateSlots`. The server markup is left as served.
entries.fix: Wire it: `wire([renderer, hydration, slots, hydrateSlots])`.

entries.message: a child applier changed identity {swaps} times at one part, so `previous` is always undefined and it restarts every render.
entries.fix: Hoist the applier — written as an object-literal method it is a new function per call: `function applyThing(part, previous) { … }` once at module scope, and `const thing = (x) => ({ _$child$: applyThing, x })` with the state on the object.

entries.message: a child position was given `{value}`, which renders as the word "{value}" — the usual cause is `${cond && …}` with a false `cond`.
entries.fix: Write `${cond ? … : null}`, or `${(cond && …) || null}`; `null` and `undefined` are the values that render nothing. If you meant to display the boolean, say so with `${String(value)}` and this goes quiet.

entries.message: {where} never reached the parsed tree — the HTML parser DROPPED the element it was written on, because its parent's content model forbids it (`<select>` takes only options, `<form>` cannot nest, and so on). {lost} binding(s) lost; the bindings AFTER it are unaffected, because each marker carries its own index.
entries.fix: Move the element out of its parent, or use one the parent can hold.

entries.message: @{name} is not an event <{tag}> fires — did you mean @{best}? (In JSX, on{name} compiles to @{name}.)
entries.fix: A custom event by this name is fine, and this is said only in development.

entries.message: a binding inside <{tag}> in SVG or MathML cannot sit beside an element there — the renderer reads <{tag}> as text and rebuilds it around its bindings, which destroys the elements in it.
entries.fix: Bind text directly in the <{tag}> (no elements), or move the element out of it.

entries.message: the value at position {position} sits inside a nested <template>'s content — inert markup that is never rendered — so it is ignored (and the server ignores it too).
entries.fix: Render into the live tree instead.

entries.message: expected a container node as the second argument and received {received}.
entries.fix: It renders *into* something — `renderInto(html`…`, document.body)`.

entries.message: a binding inside <{tag}> is never rendered — the parser reads its content as text whole, and <{tag}> is obsolete.
entries.fix: Use <pre> for preformatted text.

entries.message: threw; its error is printed beside this line, and the render continued without it.
entries.fix: Fix the ref, or wire an 'error' insert to handle what refs throw.

entries.message: <{tag}> is left OPEN by this template, so everything after it becomes its child rather than its sibling. HTML has no self-closing syntax outside <svg> and <math> — `<{tag} />` is an open tag, not an empty element.
entries.fix: Write `<{tag}></{tag}>`. (@verajs/jsx rewrites this for you; a hand-written template has to say it.)

entries.message: renders a `<slot>` into LIGHT DOM, but @verajs/renderer/slots is not wired, so nothing is distributed.
entries.fix: Wire it BEFORE anything renders: wire([renderer, slots]).

entries.message: a binding sits directly inside <table>, where the HTML parser inserts a <tbody> that a client render does not. The same template then renders as `table > tr` and parses as `table > tbody > tr`, so `table > tr` selectors match on only one path and hydration rebuilds this container instead of adopting it.
entries.fix:
Write the section explicitly — `${rows}
` — and every path agrees.

entries.message: a template cannot end inside a tag — the parser drops an unfinished tag.
entries.fix: Close the tag inside the template.

entries.message: `</{tag}>` is read by the parser as ANOTHER <{tag}>, so this template renders two where it describes one.
entries.fix: A void element has no end tag — write `<{tag}>` alone.

entries.message: <{tag}> was built as {built} and placed inside <{host}>, where it will not render.
entries.fix: {advice}

entries.message: refusing {key} — spread names arrive at runtime, which is exactly the property that makes an HTML sink unreviewable.
entries.fix: Write it in the template — html`<div .innerHTML=${trusted}>` — sanitized first (renderer README, security note).

entries.message: ignoring a props bag that is not a plain object — received {received}. A string is iterated by character index, so `spread('text')` would set attributes named 0, 1, 2 and 3; anything else applies nothing at all.
entries.fix: This is usually an import or a property that resolved to something unexpected.

entries.message: refusing {key} — an attribute name cannot contain whitespace, a quote, `<`, `>`, `/`, `=` or a control character, and one that cannot be written into markup would not survive server rendering.
entries.fix: Spread names arrive at runtime; check where this key came from.

entries.message: `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` is not available on a tag component and has been dropped. A tag binds through `spread`, whose names are only known at runtime — so it refuses `.innerHTML` outright rather than open an unreviewable HTML sink.
entries.fix: Write the element directly, with the value sanitized first: html`<${Tag} .innerHTML=${trusted}>` (see the renderer README's security note).

entries.message: only another tag may be interpolated — a string cannot become markup.
entries.fix: Interpolate a tag: tag`${Base}-card`, where Base is itself a tag.

entries.message: `key` does nothing on a tag component and has been dropped — a key marks a template for list reconciliation, and this call returns one rather than being one.
entries.fix: In JSX, write it and the compiler handles it: `<Row key=${id}>` becomes `keyed(id, Row({…}))`. Calling by hand, wrap it yourself: `keyed(id, Row({…}))`.

entries.message: {text} is not an element name. A tag names ONE element — letters, then letters, digits, '.', '_' or '-' — and nothing else becomes markup here.
entries.fix: Attributes and content belong in the template: html`<${heading} class="title">…</${heading}>`.

entries.message: a tag (`{tag}`) may only stand in tag position — `<${T}>…</${T}>`.
entries.fix: Spliced anywhere else it would become text or part of an attribute, which a tag never means.

entries.message: the key {key} is used by more than one item in this list. A key identifies one item, so which of them keeps the existing DOM is not defined — the list still renders, but nothing about which node ends up where can be relied on.
entries.fix: Give every item a key of its own — an id, not an index or a value two items share.

entries.message: expected a template as the second argument and received {received}.
entries.fix:
It marks a template with a key — `keyed(row.id, html`
  • …
    • `)`.

entries.message: threw in {phase}; its error is printed beside this line, and {outcome}.
entries.fix: Fix the claim's callback, or wire an 'error' insert to handle what claims throw.

entries.message: a 'template' hook set an instance hook before `elements` (priority 10) and is replaced.
entries.fix: Claim elements through the `element` insert instead of a second instance hook.

entries.message: this page was server-rendered and nothing hydrates it, so {outcome}.
entries.fix: Wire `hydration` beside the renderer — `wire([renderer, hydration])` — and, where a light host holds the page's content, `hydrateSlots` with `slots`: `wire([renderer, hydration, slots, hydrateSlots])`.

entries.message: {slot} carries {attributes}, which does nothing in a light-DOM component: the slot element steps out of the page while it has content.
entries.fix: Events, `name` and `&ref` all work here.

entries.message: reads the light-DOM statement through `slots`, which is not wired.
entries.fix: Wire `slots` beside it: `wire([renderer, hydration, slots, hydrateSlots])`.
